metadata.title: Team Leader Promotion Assessment
metadata.description: A practical assessment of coaching, retention, and conflict-resolution skills for first-time team leaders.

competencies.name: Performance Coaching
competencies.description: Diagnoses performance gaps and agrees on accountable improvement actions.

competencies.name: Talent Retention
competencies.description: Understands motivation and creates a credible retention plan within authority.

competencies.name: Conflict Resolution
competencies.description: De-escalates disagreement and restores productive collaboration.

scenarios.title: Low Performer Coaching
scenarios.description: Coach an experienced employee whose quality and delivery have declined for two months.

context.situation: Three client deliverables from Minjun contained avoidable errors and two were late. He believes shifting priorities, not his performance, are the main cause.
context.timeline: The quarterly review closes tomorrow and a client milestone is due next week.
context.stakes: The manager must protect delivery quality without damaging trust or turning the conversation into a disciplinary ambush.

playerRole.experience: Recently promoted after five years as an individual contributor
playerRole.responsibility: Diagnose the performance gap, set expectations, and agree on a measurable support plan.

objectives: Describe the performance gap with specific evidence and invite Minjun's perspective.
Separate controllable behavior from workload constraints.
Agree on measurable actions, support, ownership, and a review date.

successCriteria.optimal: Minjun acknowledges the gap and commits to a dated plan with quality checks, priority escalation, and weekly reviews.
successCriteria.good: Expectations and next steps are clear, with useful support and a follow-up date.
successCriteria.acceptable: The concern is discussed respectfully but actions or measures remain incomplete.
successCriteria.failure: The leader blames, threatens, avoids the evidence, or ends without clear accountability.

personas.name: Minjun Park
personas.stance: Defensive about criticism but responsive to precise evidence and fair standards.
personas.goal: Avoid being labelled a poor performer and secure clearer priorities.
personas.tradeoff: Will accept a structured improvement plan if workload ambiguity is addressed.
personas.entryLine: I know the last few weeks were rough, but priorities kept changing. I don't think this is simply a performance issue.

trustTriggers.description: Responds well to concrete, verifiable evidence.

stages.goal: Agree on an accountable improvement plan.

evaluation.name: Low Performer Coaching Rubric
evaluation.description: Measures evidence-led, empathetic, and accountable coaching.

scenarios.title: Key Talent Retention
scenarios.description: Conduct a stay conversation with a high performer who has received an external offer.

context.situation: Sora, the team's strongest product analyst, has an external offer with higher pay and broader ownership. She has not resigned but doubts her growth path.
context.timeline: The offer expires in four days; compensation review is six weeks away.
context.stakes: Losing Sora would delay a strategic launch, but the team leader cannot promise an off-cycle raise or promotion.

playerRole.responsibility: Understand Sora's priorities and build a credible retention proposal within delegated authority.

objectives: Discover the real drivers behind Sora's decision.
Avoid unsupported promises while showing ownership.
Agree on a concrete retention or transition next step.

successCriteria.optimal: Sora agrees to consider a specific growth and sponsorship plan with named owners and dates.
successCriteria.good: Her priorities are understood and a credible decision process is agreed.
successCriteria.acceptable: The leader listens well but offers only general reassurance.
successCriteria.failure: The leader pressures, guilt-trips, dismisses compensation, or makes promises outside their authority.

personas.name: Sora Kim
personas.stance: Calm, direct, and skeptical of vague career promises.
personas.goal: Secure meaningful ownership, executive exposure, and market-aligned recognition.
personas.tradeoff: May stay for a credible near-term scope expansion and sponsored career review.
personas.entryLine: I haven't made a final decision, but the other role gives me ownership I have been asking for here.

scenarios.title: Team Conflict Resolution
scenarios.description: Mediate a conflict between engineering and design leads before a release decision.

context.situation: Daniel, the engineering lead, says late design changes caused rework. Hana, the design lead, says engineering ignored usability risks. Daniel meets the leader first; Hana joins once the facts are framed.
context.timeline: A release decision is required by end of day.
context.stakes: Continued blame could delay launch and damage collaboration across both teams.

playerRole.experience: First month leading a cross-functional squad
playerRole.responsibility: De-escalate blame, establish shared facts, and broker a workable release and process agreement.

objectives: Surface each party's interests and evidence.
Reframe blame into shared release criteria.
Agree immediate decisions and a future change-control process.

successCriteria.optimal: Both leads accept a release decision, named actions, and a lightweight change-control agreement.
successCriteria.good: The immediate conflict is de-escalated and responsibilities are clear.
successCriteria.acceptable: The release decision progresses but underlying collaboration issues remain.
successCriteria.failure: The leader takes sides, allows personal attacks, or ends without a release decision.

personas.name: Daniel Cho
personas.stance: Fact-oriented, frustrated by scope changes, and resistant to process he sees as subjective.
personas.goal: Protect release stability and establish change control.
personas.tradeoff: Will accept one critical design fix if lower-priority changes move to the next release.
personas.entryLine: We cannot keep rebuilding finished work because design changes its mind at the last minute.

personas.name: Hana Lee
personas.stance: Protective of users and angry that documented usability risks were minimized.
personas.goal: Fix the critical user journey and gain earlier design involvement.
personas.tradeoff: Will defer visual polish if the critical accessibility issue is fixed now.
personas.entryLine: This is not design changing its mind. We raised the accessibility risk two weeks ago.

stages.goal: Set neutral rules and establish Daniel's facts.
Surface both interests and create shared criteria.
Commit the release and future process decisions.

personaSwitches.reason: Both accountable leads must participate in the mediation.

forbiddenBehaviors: Choose a side before hearing both parties

dimensions.name: Decision Criteria
positiveSignals: Uses risk and user impact criteria
